rules: Write original educational prose in American English. Do not copy any other website.
Do not invent statistics, quotations, clinical outcomes, author credentials, or organization history.
Separate traditional teaching, practitioner report, and modern research. Never say a practice cures disease, removes toxins, or treats anxiety or any other condition.
For Kundalini, Reiki, Ayurveda, chakras, and breathwork, state that traditional metaphysical claims are not established as scientific facts.
Open with a direct definition. Section headings must be questions ending in ? except on glossary and hub pages.
Do not put markdown headings (#) inside intro or section content. Use paragraphs and, when useful, bullet lists or bold.
Link with markdown paths that exist in this file's path list, for example [meditation](/topics/meditation/).
Use only source_ids from content/sources.json. Use only about and mentions ids from content/entities.json.
author_id is editorial-team. Dates are 2026-10-04T10:00:00-04:00. language is en-US. country is US. status is published.
featured_image and og_image are /images/{id}.svg. Alt text describes an abstract geometric illustration for that subject and does not stuff keywords.
meta_title is 45 to 65 characters. meta_description is 120 to 160 characters. canonical equals path.
Long pages (pillar, explainer, guide, comparison, misconception) need at least 1250 words, 7 sections, 3 sources, and 6 internal links.
Glossary, chakra, meditation, and yoga pages need at least 850 words, 3 sources, and 4 internal links.
Question pages need at least 650 words, 2 sources, and 3 internal links.
Set disclaimer.required to true for every misconception and for any page whose topic is kundalini, reiki, ayurveda, chakras, or breathwork.
Chakra pages must include facts keys Sanskrit name and Traditional location, and the prose must say the rainbow chart is a modern convention.
related is an array of paths. Include at least four related paths on long pages.
